chore(rollout-app): remove migrate key and simplify conditionals (#411)

## Summary
Remove the migrate functionality that was originally added as an
experiment for seamless migration from `simple-app` to `rollout-app`.
After evaluation, we've determined that the safer approach for migration
is to use parallel apps and then switch traffic, rather than the
in-place migration approach.

## Changes
- ✅ Remove `migrate` configuration from `values.yaml`
- ✅ Remove all migration-related logic from `rollout.yaml` template  
- ✅ Update documentation to remove migration references
- ✅ Combine duplicate conditionals in canary strategy for cleaner code

## Background
The `migrate` key was originally added to experiment with in-place
migration capabilities between simple-app (Deployment) and rollout-app
(Rollout). However, we're removing this unused code because the safer
approach for migration is to have parallel apps running and then perform
traffic switching once the new app is fully scaled out.

## Test plan
- [x] Verify chart renders correctly without migrate references
- [x] Confirm no breaking changes for existing rollout-app users
- [x] Test canary and blue-green strategies work as expected

commit.message:
feat(rollout-app): add Istio subset-level traffic splitting support tweaks for multi-zone rollouts (#405)

## Why

### 1. Support trafficRouting option of DestinationRule via subset
identifiers

For more fine-grained/granular traffic routing, e.g., of an existing
`Service`, if you have a `DestinationRule` that references subset
identifiers on a VirtualService, Rollouts can manage that too.


https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/networking/virtual-service/#Destination-subset

**So**: This change adds support of that ☝️ 

### 2. Multi-zone `Rollouts` create a `Rollout` per zone, which has
Istio trafficRouting limitations

**_Multiple_** `Rollouts` objects cannot:

1. point to (control) the same `stableService` or `canaryService` to
update `VirtualService` weights.
2. point to (control) the same `DestinationRule` for subset-level
traffic routing

**So**: This change ensures istio trafficRouting is not set on the
`Rollout` object for multi-zone Rollouts. With the idea that as canaries
come up they get added to the overall pod count along with stable at
each step until promoted.

## Example Diff

values.yaml:

```yaml
virtualService:
  subsetRouting:
    enabled: true

    subsets:
      - name: stable
        weight: 100
      - name: canary
        weight: 0

    canarySubsetName: canary
    stableSubsetName: stable
    destinationRuleName: my-existing-dr
```

Rendered diff from original:

```diff
@@ -840,7 +840,14 @@
             host: rollout-app
             port:
               number: 80
+            subset: stable
           weight: 100
+        - destination:
+            host: rollout-app
+            port:
+              number: 80
+            subset: canary
+          weight: 0
 ---
 # Source: rollout-app/templates/tests/test-connection.yaml
 apiVersion: v1
@@ -3824,13 +3845,15 @@
       topology.kubernetes.io/zone: us-west-2c
   strategy:
     canary:
-      stableService: samwise
-      canaryService: samwise-canary

       trafficRouting:
         istio:
           virtualService:
             name: samwise-rollout
+          destinationRule:
+            name: samwise-app-samwise
+            canarySubsetName: canary
+            stableSubsetName: stable
       canaryMetadata:
         annotations:
           ad.datadoghq.com/tags: '{"rollout_canary": "true"}'
```

commit.message:
chore(charts/nd-common): support newer trafficDistribution field in Service (#403)

# What

As of Kubernetes v1.31, `Service` spec [supports the trafficDistribution
field](https://v1-31.docs.kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#traffic-distribution)
(which is beta on v1.31.x an GA in v1.33).

For now, to ensure no side-effects, we only will set the field **_if the
user explicitly sets it_**.

```
service:
  trafficDistribution: PreferClose
```

This is a simple heuristic: for kube-proxy, this means prioritizing
sending traffic to endpoints within the same zone as the client if an
endpoint in the zone exists.

In its absence, the default routing strategy for kube-proxy is to
distribute traffic to any endpoint in the cluster

Because of its straight-forward heuristic, this can possibly lead to
overload, in which case setting the annotation of
`service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode: Auto` may be a better approach if
we want to default to something (see tests below)

# Test Results

## Setup

### Client (`debug-pod`) and Server (with trafficDistribution not set):

```
POD_NAME                   ZONE          POD_IP
debug-pod                  us-west-2b    100.80.89.20
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-5p7t8    us-west-2c    100.80.184.152
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-lrgbj    us-west-2a    100.80.58.64
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-qwwqw    us-west-2b    100.80.88.238

$ kubectl get svc httpbin -o yaml | yq '.spec.trafficDistribution'
null

$ stern httpbin > /tmp/requests.log
```

#### Expected Result

All requests from `debug-pod` should be round-robined between the 3 pods

```
~ $ for attempt in $(seq 1 20); do curl -I http://httpbin ; sleep 1 ; done
```

#### Actual Result

```
$ grep '"x_forwarded_for":"100.80.89.20' /tmp/requests.log | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c
   8 httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-5p7t8
   5 httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-lrgbj
   7 httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-qwwqw
```

### Client (`debug-pod`) and Server (with trafficDistribution set to
`PreferClose`):

```

debug-pod                  us-west-2b    100.80.89.20
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-4wxtc    us-west-2c    100.80.184.152
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-5dp9l    us-west-2a    100.80.56.159
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-bkr5z    us-west-2b    100.80.88.238

$ kubectl get svc httpbin -o yaml | yq '.spec.trafficDistribution'

$ stern httpbin > /tmp/requests.log
```

#### Expected Result

All requests from `debug-pod` should go to `httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-bkr5z`
(same zone).

```
~ $ for attempt in $(seq 1 20); do curl -I http://httpbin ; sleep 1 ; done
```

#### Actual Result

```
$ grep '"x_forwarded_for":"100.80.89.20' /tmp/requests.log | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c
  20 httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-bkr5z
```

### Client (`debug-pod`) with Service annotation
service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode: Auto

```

debug-pod                  us-west-2b    100.80.89.24
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-dj94t    us-west-2a    100.80.56.151
httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-wfzl7    us-west-2c    100.80.184.118

null

[...]

Most of the requests going to `httpbin-5f6bdcd9f-xkxkc`

commit.message:
feat(rollout-app): enabled seamless migration capabilities between simple-app and rollout-app (#402)

## Context
Currently, `simple-app` users do not have a seamless way to transition
between a regular `Deployment` kind to the `Rollout` kind that is
present within `rollout-app`. Luckily, the wonderful developers at Argo
Rollouts have already kept this into mind while developing their CRD,
and have a _built in measure_ that allows users who are using a regular
deployment strategy / Deployment primitive (aka `simple-app` users). The
[Rollout CRD accepts the `workloadRef`
field](https://argo-rollouts.readthedocs.io/en/stable/migrating/#reference-deployment-from-rollout),
which seems to be only used during migrations, so I wrapped it under a
`migrate` map field. This makes it easy for developers to find within
`rollout-app` (I expect developers to just be smart and ctrl+f the
keyword "migrate" etc.), and makes sense to me.

Also, I ensured that users of `simple-app` who are using multiple
availability zones are able to transition over as well, by ensuring that
the deployment name gets changed when looping through availability zone
names.

This is a big new feature, so I think that this warranted a minor
version bump, but I am also open towards wrapping this up in `v1.5.x` 🙌

---------

Signed-off-by: Eduardo Morales <emorales@nextdoor.com>

commit.message:
chore(charts/rollout-app): support dynamicStableScale option in canary (#386)

Adding support for `dynamicStableScale` in canary:
https://argo-rollouts.readthedocs.io/en/stable/features/canary/#dynamic-stable-scale-with-traffic-routing

When set, the rollout dynamically reduces the scale of the **stable**
ReplicaSet during an update such that it scales down as the traffic
weight increases to canary.

Advantage include:

1.  savings on spinup of new nodes in high-replica count environments
2. less likely for HPAs to scale stable down as overall pod counts stay
the same for similar traffic split when canary is being rolled out

<sub>By default the stable ReplicaSet is left scaled to 100% during the
update. This has the advantage that if an abort occurs, traffic can be
immediately shifted back to the stable ReplicaSet without delay (if set
to true, and the rollout is aborted, the canary ReplicaSet will
dynamically scale down as traffic shifts back to stable</sub>

the same for similar traffic split when canary is being rolled out

<sub>By default the stable ReplicaSet is left scaled to 100% during the
update. This has the advantage that if an abort occurs, traffic can be
immediately shifted back to the stable ReplicaSet without delay (if set
to true, and the rollout is aborted, the canary ReplicaSet will
dynamically scale down as traffic shifts back to stable</sub>

feat: integrated capabilities for multiple zones into charts/rollout-app (#384)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> For reviewers, I suggest going over the `rollout.yaml` file first to
get a better understanding of how zones are handled, what is checked,
etc. so that when reviewing the diffs to the other templates, things
make a bit more sense 🙂
## Context | Description | Why
Currently, if a user wanted to add multiple zones / add a Rollout
operator for different clusters, they would have to have multiple
instances of a Rollout CRD definition within a file / have multiple
files for each rollout on top of having to manually change and keep
track of certain fields within the `spec` in order to customize and make
each rollout service have different selectors.

This PR changes that, integrating the field `rolloutZones` to
automatically make Rollout operators for each specific zone, creating
duplicate rollout services for each one with other configurable options.
This is handy to have, for instance, if one of your configured zones
handles _substantially_ more traffic at times, and thus, can make it
such that splitting up the rollout between zones can help save some
costs.

## Testing
* running helm template showed no errors!
* I `helm install`'ed two versions of this rollout-app: one with an
empty `rolloutZones: []`, and it worked, and I also installed a version
of the app where the rolloutZones was `rolloutZones: [us-west-2a]`,
added an appropriate label to a node selector, and it worked! So,
rollout zones may need more configuration to get the node selection to
work, but otherwise, this should _not_ be a breaking change
* I also tested out the `rolloutZonesTransition` variable, and it
worked! Below is an example of how it works
* I also tested this out within the `dev1-test` cluster with a dummy
repo on a branch. To see the branch and testing, contact me so that I
can send it via slack! (since this is a public repo, I don't want to
share it here, haha)

## Videos
Contact me so that I can send the video of it working as well through
Slack!

---------

fix(nd-common): support istio-proxy native sidecar (initContainer) preStop override (#361)

## Why

### Context

[Kubernetes native sidecar
containers](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/)
run as `InitContainers`

Istio allows us to [run the proxy as a native
sidecar](https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/48794).

### What This Change Does

Allows preStop commands to be set on initContainers as well.

### But Why Is This Change Needed?

Ideally, the [default
/drain](https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/14c3ef57a77fd4995f84bac71b41a768564714a9/manifests/charts/istio-control/istio-discovery/files/injection-template.yaml#L211-L220)
on native sidecars should suffice.

However, an open bug (https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/51855) is
forcing us to potentially bring our default preStop commands on the
native sidecars as well.

## Diffs

### Diff between default values and setting
`istio.nativeSidecarsEnabled: true`

**When to use**: This is the proposed ideal setting when we want a
workaround to https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/51855

```diff
@@ -234,7 +234,7 @@
         traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeInboundPorts: "9090"
         proxy.istio.io/overrides: >-
           {
-            "containers": [
+            "initContainers": [
               {
                 "name": "istio-proxy",
                 "lifecycle": {
```

### Diff between default values and setting
`istio.nativeSidecarsEnabled: true` and `preStopDefaultEnabled: false`

**When to use**: This is the proposed ideal setting when
https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/51855 is fixed and we want to
default to upstream/Istio's drain mechanism... i.e., no override

```diff
@@ -232,25 +232,6 @@
         checksum/secrets: c8fa9ff9cda8a0e2d93fdc712c82373c94a1a5f1a48fc6d8db9f978047d937b6
         proxy.istio.io/config: '<redacted>'
         traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeInboundPorts: "9090"
-        proxy.istio.io/overrides: >-
-          {
-            "containers": [
-              {
-                "name": "istio-proxy",
-                "lifecycle": {
-                  "preStop": {
-                    "exec": {
-                      "command": [
-                        "/bin/sh",
-                        "-c",
-                        "while [ $(netstat -plunt | grep tcp | egrep -v 'envoy|pilot-agent' | wc -l | xargs) -ne 0 ]; do sleep 1; done"
-                      ]
-                    }
-                  }
-                }
-              }
-            ]
-          }
         ad.datadoghq.com/simple-app.check_names: '["prometheus"]'
         ad.datadoghq.com/simple-app.init_configs: '[{}]'
         ad.datadoghq.com/simple-app.instances: |-
```

commit.message:
feat: analogous AuthorizationPolicies to NetworkPolicies for (Istio) multi-cluster access (#342)

## What this change does

In essence:

- If service has Istio enabled, adds `AuthorizationPolicy` that is
_**analogous**_ to the existing `NetworkPolicy` that we already create
(**this should be a no-op**).
- If service also enables
~`.Values.network.multiCluster.allowFromRemote`~
`.Values.network.allowAll`, we open up the NetworkPolicy to allow the
AuthorizationPolicies above to take over its enforcement wholly.

## Why

To enable services in a multi-primary (Istio mesh), mult-cluster setup
to be accessed from services in a different cluster (because
NetworkPolicies can't enforce Ingress from **outside** the Kubernetes
cluster without getting to CIDR ranges - i.e., it only knows about
cluster-local namespaces. So, we allow all and instead restrict with
Istio's AuthorizationPolicy)

commit.message:
feat: enable maintenance mode (or custom HTTP fault injections) (#338)

Similar to `retries`, this PR allows users to inject custom `faults` too
to their `VirtualService`:
https://istio.io/latest/docs/reference/config/networking/virtual-service/#HTTPFaultInjection

We also support an opinionated fault injection called `maintenanceMode`:
this will create a 100% abort fault injection to abstract away the
implementation from end users (it also [implicitly deactivates the
HPA](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/#implicit-maintenance-mode-deactivation)
while in maintenance mode)

The templates are smart enough to only render if either one of
`maintenanceMode.enabled` or `faults` are set.

feat(simple-app): Add secretsEngine support for Sealed Secrets (#261)

## Why

We have secretsEngine for:

-  `plaintext` (for regular k8s resource "Secret")
- `kms` (for resource "KMSSecret").

This adds secretsEngine support for `sealed` (for resource
"SealedSecret" from [Bitnami Sealed
Secrets](https://github.com/bitnami-labs/sealed-secrets)).

## Test

### Original values.test.yaml

```
secretsEngine: plaintext
secrets:
  foo: bar
```

### New values.test.yaml (after generating a sealed secret)

```
secretsEngine: sealed
secrets:
  foo: 
```

### Helm Diff

```diff
--- /tmp/orig.yaml	2024-02-12 06:41:52
+++ /tmp/new.yaml	2024-02-12 09:25:54
@@ -47,14 +47,6 @@
     app.kubernetes.io/name: simple-app
     app.kubernetes.io/instance: simple-app
 ---
-# Source: simple-app/templates/secret.yaml
-apiVersion: v1
-kind: Secret
-metadata:
-  name: simple-app-secrets
-data:
-  FOO: YmFy
----
 # Source: simple-app/templates/service.yaml
 apiVersion: v1
 kind: Service
@@ -133,7 +125,7 @@
     metadata:
       annotations:
         kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container: simple-app
-        checksum/secrets: 07091d9e7b63ac86966e39652ca5327568145ae7b61a16b7d5df29f918641ea5
+        checksum/secrets: e1bd14a428065781359d65795d0ea11920771ee40496a45146eadab793817c5d
         proxy.istio.io/config: '{ "holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts": true }'
         traffic.sidecar.istio.io/excludeInboundPorts: "9090"
         proxy.istio.io/overrides: >-
@@ -488,6 +480,20 @@
           namespace: simple-app
           name: simple-app
           instance: simple-app
+---
+# Source: simple-app/templates/sealedsecret.yaml
+apiVersion: bitnami.com/v1alpha1
+kind: SealedSecret
+metadata:
+  name: simple-app-secrets
+  annotations:
+    sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/namespace-wide: "true"
+spec:
+  encryptedData:
+    FOO: ""
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      name: simple-app-secrets
 ---
 # Source: simple-app/templates/servicemonitor.yaml
 apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
```

### Applied SealedSecret

```
$ k get sealedsecret
NAME                 STATUS   SYNCED   AGE
simple-app-secrets            True     15m

$ k get secret
NAME                        TYPE                DATA   AGE
simple-app-secrets          Opaque              1      16m

$ k get secret simple-app-secrets -o yaml | yq .data
FOO: YmFy // <-- "bar" in base64
```

commit.message:
feat(simple-app,rollout-app,stateful-app): support multiple namespaces for gateways (#216)

The existing code made it difficult (impossible) to support moving from a `Gateway` in `ns1` to another one in `ns2`. It also assumed that `Gateway` objects lived in `istio-system` which is specifically against the [best practices in the Istio guide](https://istio.io/latest/docs/setup/additional-setup/gateway/#deploying-a-gateway) where they are recommended to live in a dedicated namespace.

This PR introduces a **breaking change** to the `rollout-app`, `statefull-app`, and `simple-app` charts to reformat the way the `VirtualService` object's `.spec.gateways` field is managed. I have introduced a loud `fail()` message to ensure that you cannot upgrade the chart without making the appropriate change.

[all charts] Fix some bad ContainerWaiting/CrashLoop Rules (#168)

The rules we had in place to catch Pods in a CrashLoopBackoff state were
too complicated and easily missed pods depending on the situation. A
much cleaner metric exists with a very clear selector for
`CrashLoopBackOff`, so I am rewriting the rules to use that.

commit.message:
[simple-app/statefull-app/daemonset-app] Always use a Service (#160)

**What did I want?**

We discovered
(https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/39792#issuecomment-1189669761)
that Istio requires a `Service` point to all workloads (clients and
servers) in order to generate their "locality" information. Without a
`Service` pointing to the workload, Istio will not  generate this
locality information and we cannot leverage zone-aware routing.

**What did I do?**

All of our apps now create a `Service` resource no matter what that
points to the pods that are running. The `Service` does not need to be
exposed (meaning that no `NetworkPolicy` is created if the
`.Values.ports` key is empty), but we create the `Service` anyways so
that Istio can determine locality for all workloads.

commit.message:
[rollout-app] New Argo Rollouts based Deployment (#136)

**What did I want?**

As we begin using [Argo Rollouts](https://argoproj.github.io/argo-rollouts/) - we need a new default application template that can create the `Rollout` objects, as well as the more customized `VirtualService` and `Service` resources. I wanted to enable us to begin experimenting with these deployment models in a simple way.

**What did I do?**

A newly created `rollout-app` chart has been created along with some customization to the Github Workflow. The workflow now detects if the `rollout-app` chart was updated, and if it was, we then install the Argo Rollouts controller/CRD for the tests. When the tests run, we verify that we can create both a `BlueGreen` and `Canary` rollout resource type. We are explicitly not testing actually triggering a rollout - we don't need to test the fundamental behavior of Argo, just that our chart basically works.
